clue.text: Lively procedure for maintaining discipline!

definitions.meaning: a brisk, vigorous pace can be called a ... one
smacking a child's bottom as a punishment, an old way of keeping order

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek remark that a brisk punishment keeps everyone in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanking is both an adjective for brisk or vigorous and the noun for smacking as a punishment.

clue.text: Before broadcast, books are taken over city

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: turned over, so the pair of pieces read backwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Ahead of transmission, some books are seized by a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' reverses AIR and OT together, giving TORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is a city in South Africa, its administrative capital.

clue.text: Like life of knight dealing with bad blood right away

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
on means about or concerning

indicators.note: sent away means taken out of the word for bad blood

parts.note: friction is conflict or ill feeling between people

explanation.surface: A knight's life of feuding, cleared of resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like life' is fair because factual writing, such as a biography, describes real life.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonfiction writing deals with real events and people, true to life rather than invented.

clue.text: Elusive Iberian leaders snarled up outside

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: intangle is an old variant of entangle, to snarl up
the first two letters of Iberian lead it

explanation.surface: Slippery Spanish and Portuguese chiefs get caught in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the opening pair of letters, IB, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intangible cannot be grasped or pinned down, so it is elusive.

clue.text: Sort of stop swallowing tea, say, when speaking

definitions.text: Sort of stop swallowing tea, say, when speaking

parts.words: Sort of stop swallowing tea, say, when speaking
parts.note: a consonant made by closing the throat, which speakers use in place of a T sound, so the T is lost

explanation.surface: Someone stops drinking tea to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pause from drinking; the 'stop' is phonetic, the throat-made sound that replaces a T in 'wa'er' for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A glottal stop is the sound made by closing the vocal cords, often heard in place of T.

clue.text: Surplus port duke abandoned

indicators.note: the duke is left behind, taken out of the port

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A duke leaves the port with goods to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean left over, in excess or surplus.

clue.text: Soldiers' bash on island, one in South Pacific

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
to bash is to hit

explanation.surface: Troops hold a party on an island in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' suggests a party, and 'island' looks like part of the definition; it supplies I, leaving 'one in South Pacific' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is one of the islands of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Prisoner French marshal beheaded and cast in river

indicators.note: thrown into the river, so the marshal goes inside its name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter goes

parts.note: Philippe Pétain was a Marshal of France

explanation.surface: A captive French marshal is decapitated and thrown into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is someone held in custody, a prisoner.

clue.text: Purchase newspaper during formal reception

indicators.note: one piece sits within the time span of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a levee is a formal reception, originally one held by a monarch on rising
a rag is a slang word for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone buys a paper at a smart reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like a verb about buying; it is the noun meaning mechanical grip or advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase in the sense of a firm hold or mechanical advantage is a synonym of leverage.

clue.text: Herb or Arnold, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the entry is said the same as the surname of the person named, though spelt differently

parts.note: Arnold Bennett was an English novelist, author of The Old Wives' Tale

explanation.surface: Asks whether the man is called Herb or Arnold, judging by his name's sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' poses as a first name beside Arnold; it is the definition, the plant herb bennet (wood avens). Arnold Bennett's surname has a double T.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb bennet, also called wood avens, is a wild plant of the rose family once used medicinally.

clue.text: Cat in a cart touring continent

indicators.note: travelling about suggests the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat riding in a cart is taken round a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica is the ice-covered continent around the South Pole.

clue.text: Small reptile caught by bird in Arabian legend

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the roc is the giant bird of the Arabian Nights tales

explanation.surface: A little lizard is snatched by a mythical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals the shortened form of the reptile's name rather than its size.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the clipped informal word for a crocodile, so 'small' points to the short form.

clue.text: School boy joined by language specialist

parts.note: a grammar school is a selective British secondary school
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A schoolboy teams up with a linguist.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammarian is an expert in the rules and structure of a language.

clue.text: Shirker in African state damaged green revolution at first

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: broken up, so these letters are reordered
only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A slacker in Africa has spoilt the start of a green revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' makes NGERE from GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A malingerer feigns illness to avoid work, a shirker.

clue.text: Chastened, rule from resort outside Home Counties

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the other piece
to re-sort is to sort again, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, contains the Home Counties around London

explanation.surface: Humbled, someone governs from a seaside resort outside London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' poses as a holiday town; read as re-sort, it rearranges RULE FROM to REMORFUL, split around SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chastened is humbled and sorry, which is to say full of regret.

clue.text: Instrument doctor used to probe Olivia's woman

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so one piece is pushed into the other

parts.note: Maria is Olivia's waiting-gentlewoman in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor uses some instrument to examine Olivia's maid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' first suggests a medical tool alongside the doctor; it is the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The marimba is a percussion instrument like a large xylophone with resonators.

clue.text: Rubber tyre ultimately put into widespread service?

indicators.note: placed inside the phrase for general use

parts.note: mass use means widespread employment of something

indicators.note: only the final letter of tyre is taken

explanation.surface: Rubber tyres finally come into general use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' looks like the material of a tyre; it means one who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse gives massages, so she is literally a rubber of muscles.

clue.text: Something especially prized by mature birds?

definitions.text: Something especially prized by mature birds?

parts.note: a plum is a choice, much-coveted thing, as in a plum job
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Wonders what grown-up birds value above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the feathers adult birds take pride in.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is a bird's covering of feathers, which mature birds display and value.

clue.text: Inclination to change reading time

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A tendency to alter one's reading time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' suggests a leaning of mind; here it is a slope. 'to change' makes GRADIEN from READING.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, the degree of inclination of a surface.

clue.text: Musical skill Scot is showing in Melbourne, for example

indicators.note: appearing within, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: Lord Melbourne was a British prime minister, a PM
Ian is a typical Scottish boy's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman displays musical talent in an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Melbourne poses as the Australian city; it is Lord Melbourne, Queen Victoria's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianism is skill or technique in playing the piano.

clue.text: Like Edmund's works, Sir Patrick's are in translation

parts.note: Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of a famous Scottish ballad

indicators.note: rendering words anew suggests their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Compares Edmund's writings with Sir Patrick's in translated form.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund is Edmund Spenser, poet of The Faerie Queene. ARE IN rearranged by 'translation' gives ERIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenserian describes things in the manner of the poet Edmund Spenser, such as his stanza form.

clue.text: Like a horse endlessly decorated with spangles

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: sequined means adorned with sequins or spangles

explanation.surface: A horse is covered all over with glittering spangles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' suggests without limit; it strips S and D from the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means of or relating to horses.

clue.text: It's sometimes used to bind a work horse

definitions.text: It's sometimes used to bind a work
definitions.meaning: a soft sheepskin leather used in bookbinding
a horse whose coat is mixed with white hairs

explanation.surface: Something occasionally used to tie up a working horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work horse' reads as one phrase, but splits: 'a work' is a book, and 'horse' is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roan is both a bookbinding leather and a horse with a coat flecked with white.

clue.text: Speculator's spoilt niece with energy and high spirits

indicators.note: taken here as holding, so the speculator's word is kept within the other letters
something spoilt is damaged, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a bull is a stock-market speculator who buys expecting prices to rise

explanation.surface: A speculator's pampered niece is full of energy and cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is read as 'having', so the speculator is held within; 'spoilt' rearranges the relative to EIENC. A bull buys shares expecting prices to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullience is exuberant cheerfulness, a state of high spirits and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Smooth fellow keeping one up

indicators.note: in a down entry the one is placed at the top, above the fellow

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A suave man holds one in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' looks like an adjective for a suave fellow; it is the verb, to press clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron is to press clothes smooth with a heated appliance.

clue.text: Beam, seeing person on floating logs

definitions.meaning: a sloping timber supporting a roof
someone who travels on a raft of lashed logs

explanation.surface: A wooden beam is likened to someone riding a log raft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is a roof beam, and literally one who rafts is someone on a raft of logs.

clue.text: Legislators are not represented on board

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one boards

indicators.note: presented again in a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Politicians on a committee say they are not being represented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the standard crossword way to put letters inside the steamship abbreviation; 'represented' rearranges the three-letter and two-letter words.
explanation.definitionFit: Senators are members of a senate, a legislative chamber.

clue.text: Ethical behaviour kindled in old Scottish county

indicators.note: the lit piece is placed inside the county's name

parts.note: Moray is a former county in north-east Scotland
a kindled fire has been lit

explanation.surface: Good conduct was sparked off in an old Scottish county.
explanation.definitionFit: Morality is principled conduct, behaviour judged by standards of right and wrong.
